THE ESSENTIALS

What is an ITIN?

An Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is a tax processing number issued by the IRS for non-residents who need a US taxpayer ID but are ineligible for a Social Security Number (SSN).

If you receive royalties from platforms like Amazon KDP, earn income that is subject to US withholding tax, or need to file a personal US tax return (1040-NR) to claim a refund, the IRS requires you to have an ITIN. It acts as your personal financial identifier within the US tax system.

Common Use Cases

  • Tax Treaties: Claiming 0% withholding on royalties (Amazon/Upwork).
  • Personal Banking: Opening personal accounts or building US credit.
  • Tax Filing: Filing Form 1040-NR to report US-sourced income.
THE CHALLENGE

The Nightmare of W-7 Filings

Applying for an ITIN on your own is one of the most notoriously difficult IRS processes for non-residents.

Mailing Your Passport

If you apply directly, the IRS legally requires you to mail your original, physical passport to Texas. It will be held for months, and occasionally, passports are lost in the mail.

High Rejection Rates

Form W-7 requires you to cite specific exceptions, tax treaty articles, and attach supporting documentation. A single checked box error leads to an automatic 10-week rejection.

30% Withholding Loss

Without an ITIN, US platforms like Amazon will automatically withhold 30% of your earnings for taxes. Getting an ITIN is the only way to claim treaty benefits to reduce this to 0%.

How It Works

Intake & Reason

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

An Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is a tax processing number issued by the IRS to individuals who are required to have a US taxpayer identification number but who do not have, and are not eligible to obtain, a Social Security Number (SSN).

You may need an ITIN if you are required to file a US federal tax return, claim a tax treaty benefit, open a personal US bank account, or if you earn income from US platforms like Amazon KDP, Upwork, or personal PayPal that withhold taxes.

No. You do not need an ITIN or SSN to form a US LLC or to obtain an EIN for your business. An ITIN is strictly for personal tax purposes, whereas an EIN is for business purposes.

The IRS typically takes 7 to 11 weeks to process an ITIN application (Form W-7). During peak tax season (January - April), it can take even longer.

Normally yes, but ADVAQ partners with IRS Certifying Acceptance Agents (CAAs). This allows us to certify your passport copy, meaning you do NOT have to mail your original, physical passport to the IRS.

Yes. While a business bank account requires an EIN, opening a personal US bank account (or applying for certain US personal credit cards) often requires an ITIN if you don't have an SSN.

Not necessarily. An ITIN is just a processing number. Your tax liability depends on the source of your income and whether you are engaged in a US Trade or Business. However, an ITIN allows you to file returns to claim exemptions or treaty benefits.

Form W-7 is the official IRS application form for the Individual Taxpayer Identification Number.

ITINs expire if they are not used on a federal tax return for three consecutive years. The IRS also periodically expires older ITINs based on their middle digits.

No. An ITIN does not authorize you to work in the US, nor does it provide eligibility for Social Security benefits or the Earned Income Tax Credit.
